procedures.procedure_name: Purpose and principles of disciplinary procedures
procedures.description: Allegations of misconduct must be addressed fairly, consistently, promptly and impartially, while respecting the rights, dignity and confidentiality of everyone involved.

procedures.description: A College Disciplinary Committee (CDC) shall exist in each College to consider and determine cases of non-academic student misconduct in accordance with the Code.

procedures.description: The CDC considers allegations, assesses available evidence, determines whether misconduct has occurred and imposes appropriate corrective or disciplinary measures under the Code. It may seek legal consultation where necessary, inform parents or guardians and relevant employers where appropriate, and forward final disciplinary orders to the Registry.

procedures.description: Cases of academic dishonesty shall be dealt with in accordance with the provisions of the Wheel of Academic Law.

procedures.description: A complaint or allegation of misconduct made by a student, staff member or member of the public shall be submitted in writing to the Student Services Officer (SSO) of the respective College.

procedures.description: The SSO reviews the complaint and may address minor matters through suitable corrective measures within their authority. Cases that cannot be resolved at the SSO level are referred to the Dean of Student Affairs (DSA). Cases that cannot be resolved at the DSA level, or warrant formal disciplinary proceedings, are referred to the CDC.

procedures.description: A student against whom an allegation is made must be informed of the nature and details of the allegation and given an opportunity to respond and present relevant evidence before a disciplinary decision is made.

procedures.description: The CDC shall convene and communicate its decision within 10 working days of receiving the case, where practical. If additional time is required, reasons for the delay must be recorded and the student informed of the revised timeframe. The decision, findings, reasons and any measures imposed must be communicated in writing to the student and, where applicable, the parent or guardian.

procedures.description: Records of complaints, findings and measures imposed must be maintained in accordance with University records management requirements. Where suspension or expulsion is imposed, the student shall be handed over to the parent or guardian. A student may appeal a CDC decision to the UDC within 10 working days of receiving the decision.

procedures.procedure_name: University Disciplinary Committee and appeal submission
procedures.description: The UDC considers appeals against CDC decisions relating to non-academic misconduct. Academic appeals are considered by the University Academic Appeals Committee. An appeal must be submitted in writing to the UDC Member Secretary within 10 working days of receiving the CDC decision. It must include the appellant's name, contact address, telephone number, grounds for appeal and supporting evidence or documents.

procedures.description: An appeal may be made on one or more of the following grounds: an error in interpreting or applying the Code; a material procedural irregularity that may have affected fairness or the outcome; failure to consider relevant evidence or unreasonable exclusion of relevant evidence; or a disciplinary measure that is unreasonable or disproportionate to the nature and seriousness of the misconduct.

procedures.description: The Member Secretary shall convene the UDC within 10 working days of the appeal. The UDC may review relevant records, evidence, proceedings and the CDC decision, and may seek clarification or additional information from relevant persons.

procedures.description: The UDC may uphold the CDC decision and dismiss the appeal, refer the matter back to the CDC for reconsideration with appropriate directions, or reverse or alter the CDC decision. The Member Secretary shall communicate the UDC decision in writing to the appellant within 5 working days of the decision, with a copy to the President of the respective College.
